sentence: This project develops assays made from demineralized bone paper to study human bone metabolism and help develop drugs that slow bone aging.
This project studies how two inhibitory receptors on T cells work together to enforce tolerance to tumors in mouse tumor models.
This project tries to find out which host proteins a serine protease from Staphylococcus aureus targets and how it is activated.
This project studies how nanoparticles can deliver drugs across the blood-nerve barrier to injured nerves in the peripheral nervous system.
This project tests whether words that prehospital clinicians use for first impressions of a patient can help an artificial intelligence system support treatment decisions.
This project looks for mosaic genetic variants in patients with suspected inborn errors of immunity who lack a molecular diagnosis.
This project tries to find out which transcription factors are needed for human motor neuron differentiation.
This project builds and shares rat, mouse and cell line models for cystic kidney disease research.
This project studies how a protein on chorionic trophoblasts leads CD8 T cells to become active and damage cells during chronic chorioamnionitis.
This project tests whether Salmonella derived outer membrane vesicles with fusion proteins help CD8+ T cells control HPV-associated head and neck cancer in a model.
This project studies how genetic mutations change gene activity in retinal organoid models of spinocerebellar ataxia type 7, a disease affecting vision and motor functions.
This project tries to find out the roles of understudied human membrane proteins.
This project builds a cloud-based module that covers data preparation, model building and interpretation for biomedical researchers using artificial intelligence.
This project studies how glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists affect cognitive function, using surveys, wearable data and continuous glucose monitoring.
This project upgrades an MRI scanner used for preclinical research on cancer biology, neuroscience and immunology.
This project studies what individual spliceosomal proteins do in haploid human cells to understand human gene expression.
This project studies what risk factors lead to nociplastic pain after cardiac surgery followed by critical care.
This project studies how a transmembrane protein that is lost with age changes T cell activation and responses through T cell receptor signaling.
This project studies whether biophysical traits of brain cancer cells show how resistant they are to radiation, and targets them with extracellular vesicle drug delivery.
This project studies how genetic differences and environment change gene activity in tissue macrophages during metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
